cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: I Started the Spiral
cards.instruction: Hide how much your own fear or resentment created the emotional crisis while helping everyone calm it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've emptied the club-money envelope like you. Accounts finished. We can tell everyone to stop worrying.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I put the money in the bank bag. You saw my empty envelope and phoned saying the treasurer had stolen it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, ready for the bank. I'll tell you first that it's all accounted for; could you pass that on?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I told the whole committee you were crying about theft.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll call them together. Introduce it as a routine balance update, and I'll give them the total.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 empties own envelope as accounts completion, but B2 says A previously panicked at empty envelope; why A now copies it as completion is underexplained. D109 concealment after accusation remains clear.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 bank-bag correction leads A3 ready-for-bank; B4 committee spread causes A5 group update, but copied act and earlier panic are not one clean causal sequence.

relationship.evidence: B2 identifies accusation and B4 reports its spread.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 audience to give total without replaying fear.

specificity.evidence: A1 money removed but destination unstated; B2 only locates B money.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 routine-update request is purposeful, but setup overcomplicates source of panic.
